note: Per-case configuration for the cross-language comparison and the golden-hash anchor.
'cases' gives per-case tolerances in units in the last place. The default is 0: R and
Python must agree bit for bit. A non-zero entry is allowed only where the response family
applies a transcendental to the linear predictor. IEEE-754 requires correct rounding for
+, -, *, / and sqrt, but not for exp(), log() or pow(), and R for Windows (MinGW-w64) and
CPython (UCRT) do not share a libm. On Linux, where CI runs, they do, and every case agrees
at 0 ulp there.
control_rt_as_gaussian.json is the control that pins this down: it is crossed_mixed_rt with
the family switched to gaussian, so it consumes an identical RNG stream and an identical
linear predictor. It agrees bit for bit, which leaves exp() as the only possible source of
the residual difference in the shifted_lognormal original.
Measured on Windows 11 with R 4.6.1 and Python 3.13, R's and CPython's exp() returned
different doubles for 0.47% of 700,000 arguments and log() for 0.13% of 700,000, never by
more than 1 ulp. The 8-ulp allowance leaves headroom for a third platform's libm while
staying far below any statistically meaningful difference (~1.8e-15 relative). A logic
error would show as a much larger gap, as a differing row count, or as a differing
non-numeric cell, all of which still fail.
stress_exgaussian is currently exact on this platform, but its value path applies log() to a
uniform draw, so it belongs to the same class as the two lognormal cases and is classified
with them rather than on the accident of one seed agreeing.
beta_boundary_rounded rounds a low and a high mean to three decimals, so that values land
on 0 and 1 and are moved inside the interval by the rule in SPEC.md. Both of its Beta shapes
stay at 1 or above, which keeps the pow() of the Gamma sampler's boost out of its noround
dump. On Windows, R's ^ and CPython's ** differed by 1 ulp on 0.13% of 200,000 such
exponents.
'transcendental' lists every dump whose bytes pass through exp(), log() or pow() on the way
to the file, whether or not the case currently hashes identically across platforms. Those
bytes are libm-specific, so the cases are excluded from the golden-hash anchor, and their
cross-language comparison on the CI platform (at the ulp allowance above, 0 by default)
still gates them. The rounded .asis dumps of the exp-family cases are listed too: rounding
has quantised the libm differences away on every platform measured so far, but the digits
being rounded are still libm-specific, so anchoring them would pin an accident rather than
a guarantee.
The anchor pins the Gaussian cases, and on observed agreement, not by construction. Every
normal comes from AS 241, whose tail branch calls log() for about 15% of draws, and on
Windows about 1.5e-5 of normal draws differ between R and Python, by 1 to 3 ulp. The
anchored cases are small enough to have met no such draw on Linux or Windows. A case of
50,000 draws or more is listed here even when it is Gaussian, and compare.py refuses to
anchor a case of 50,000 rows or more, since each row draws at least one normal.
